findings.summary: Memory benchmark has no reproducer and doesn't say compiled vs pure Python; under the mypyc build __slots__ likely saves nothing
Body's claim of removed intermediate allocations is unsupported: r0|r1 allocates the same, extend((a,b)) adds a tuple, [1:] adds a copy
Most of the diff is unrelated refactors and stylistic rewrites bundled with the slots change; cut down to slots and split the rest
used_names only half removed: writer and slot remain
No evidence the mypyc build was built and tested; dataclass slots and ABC are fragile under mypyc
eq=False and repr=False change behavior and save no memory
Some new __slots__ are no-ops because base classes lack slots
update_sibling_maps made bigger for no gain, with a wrong comment
Leaf.__init__ now treats explicit empty prefix differently (prefix or self._prefix)
Node.__init__ docstring stale and children list no longer copied

why: Finding 3 says most of the diff is separate refactors and style rewrites that should be split from the slots change, and finding 1 notes the memory claim doesn't hold under mypyc, which together match the maintainer's no-focus, many-opinionated-changes reason.
